records.ymmt: 1995-2005 | Buick | LeSabre | Custom, Limited, 90th Anniversary, Celebration | 3.8L L36 (Series II/III)
records.title: LeSabre 3800 V6 Lower Intake Manifold (LIM) Gasket Leak
records.howToFix: LIM gasket job is the same: Fel-Pro MS98003T or similar updated design — $400-$800. Replace UIM plenum if cracked, and drain Dex-Cool. Many shops will replace the EGR stovepipe gasket and throttle body gasket while everything is apart.
records.repairItems: Lower intake manifold gasket; inspect/replace upper intake plenum; drain coolant; optional EGR stovepipe and throttle-body gaskets
destinations: Fel-Pro MS98014T intake manifold gasket set
records.reason: The named MS98003T is a 3.1/3.4L application. MS98014T is the verified 3800 gasket. The product does not cover the optional plenum or ancillary gaskets.
records.correction: Replace MS98003T with MS98014T. Narrow verified link scope to 1996-2005; hold 1995 until its exact engine/VIN split is confirmed.

records.ymmt: 1995-2005 | Buick | Park Avenue | Base, Ultra | 3.8L L36 (Series II/III), 3.8L L67 Supercharged
records.title: Park Avenue 3800 V6 Lower Intake Manifold (LIM) Gasket Leak
records.howToFix: Replace LIM gasket with updated Fel-Pro MS98003T (improved metal-reinforced design) — $400-$800 at independent. Replace upper intake plenum at the same time if cracked. Drain Dex-Cool and refill with Zerex G-05 or compatible HOAT. Inspect oil for coolant contamination at every change; milky oil means immediate teardown.
records.repairItems: Lower intake manifold gasket; inspect/replace upper intake plenum; drain/refill coolant; inspect oil contamination
destinations: Fel-Pro MS98014T intake manifold gasket set
1995-2005 Park Avenue 3.8L; confirm naturally aspirated vs supercharged configuration and VIN
records.reason: MS98014T is the correct 3800 lower-intake set; MS98003T is not. The optional upper plenum and coolant choice remain separate decisions.
records.correction: Replace MS98003T with MS98014T. Remove the blanket recommendation to replace Dex-Cool with Zerex G-05 unless supported by the service information for the exact vehicle.

records.ymmt: 2016-2019 | Buick | Cascada | Base, Premium, Sport Touring | 1.6L Turbo SIDI
records.title: Cascada 1.6L Turbo (Opel SIDI) Timing Chain & Carbon Buildup
records.howToFix: Chain kit replacement ~$1,500-$2,500 (parts harder to source than US-built GM engines). Walnut blast intake valves at the same service ($300-$500). Use dexos2 full-synthetic 5W-30 — required spec for European-build engines.
records.repairItems: Timing chain, guides, tensioner and remaining kit hardware; walnut-blast service; dexos2 5W-30
records.reason: Each OEM component has exact Cascada fitment, but these three links are not a complete kit. Walnut blasting is a service, not a product substitute.
records.correction: Label every component as partial. Do not present a turbocharger, scanner, or a single timing component as the complete repair.

records.title: 6T70/6T75 Transmission Wave Plate Failure
records.howToFix: Disassemble and rebuild the transmission with an updated/stronger wave plate, plus replace damaged hard parts and clean out debris; in severe cases a remanufactured unit is installed.
records.repairItems: Updated 3-5-R wave plate/drum repair; damaged hard parts; debris cleanout; possible remanufactured transmission
records.reason: The Sonnax kit addresses the wave-plate/drum failure but does not cover all hard-part damage, converter damage, labor, programming, or debris cleanout.
records.correction: Gate by transmission ID and diagnosis. Route to a transmission specialist; do not imply that buying one kit completes the rebuild.

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption / Engine Failure on 3.6L
records.howToFix: Diagnose per GM PIP5084; remedies range from PCV/oil-control updates to, in severe consumption or block-failure cases, engine replacement (around $6,500). Check oil frequently between changes as a stopgap.
records.repairItems: Diagnosis per GM PIP5084; PCV/oil-control updates if applicable; possible engine replacement
records.reason: The remedy ranges from updates to complete engine replacement. No single part can be recommended until the consumption/block failure is diagnosed.
records.correction: Keep commerce off until diagnosis identifies the failed component. A service/dealer locator is appropriate.

records.title: HVAC Blend Door Actuator Failure
records.howToFix: Replace the failed blend-door actuator and recalibrate the HVAC system. Some actuators are easy to reach; others require significant dash disassembly, which drives up labor.
records.repairItems: Failed HVAC actuator at the diagnosed position; HVAC recalibration
destinations: 2008-2013 Enclave; confirm actuator position by VIN
2013-2017 Enclave 3.6L; confirm actuator position by VIN
records.reason: The Enclave has multiple HVAC actuators that are not interchangeable. The failed position must be diagnosed before purchase; recalibration remains a service step.
records.correction: Display a mandatory position/VIN check. Never label either actuator as fitting every HVAC-door location.

records.title: Loss of Power Steering Assist (Pump Wear)
records.howToFix: Replace the power steering pump (and inspect/replace fluid and lines). Covered under GM Special Coverage for 10yr/150k mi on affected vehicles; otherwise replace the pump out of pocket.
records.repairItems: Power-steering pump; inspect fluid and lines; Special Coverage eligibility check
records.reason: Coverage/VIN check comes before retail. The pump link does not include fluid, lines, steering gear work, or labor.
records.correction: Set recallFirst/coverage-first behavior and make the retail pump secondary.

records.ymmt: 2008-2011 | Buick | Enclave | CX, CXL, CXL-1, CXL-2 | all
records.title: Enclave Power Steering Assist Loss — Special Coverage Adjustment 14329
records.howToFix: Confirm Special Coverage 14329 eligibility at any GM/Buick dealer with your VIN. If still within 10 years and 150,000 miles, remedy is free: dealer flushes power-steering system, replaces the PS pump, and installs a new steering-gear valve housing. If out of the coverage window, expect $700-$1,400 for the same job at an independent.
records.repairItems: VIN eligibility; dealer flush; pump; steering-gear valve housing as directed by Special Coverage 14329
records.reason: The How to Fix explicitly calls for VIN-based coverage and a multi-step dealer remedy. A generic pump link would omit the flush and valve-housing work.
records.correction: Use official coverage/dealer routing. Do not place a buy-parts CTA ahead of the VIN check.

records.title: Rear A/C Evaporator Corrosion & Refrigerant Leaks
records.howToFix: Recover the refrigerant, replace the corroded rear evaporator (and rear blower motor if shedding debris) or the leaking line, then evacuate and recharge the system. Confirm leak source with dye/UV before recharging.
records.repairItems: Leak diagnosis with dye/UV; auxiliary evaporator or leaking line; rear blower if debris-damaged; refrigerant recover/evacuate/recharge
destinations: only if auxiliary core leak is confirmed
records.reason: The TSB identifies auxiliary-evaporator corrosion, but the How to Fix also allows a line or blower failure. Refrigerant work requires proper recovery equipment.
records.correction: Require leak-source confirmation before showing the core as the repair. Do not reuse this link for a leaking line or blower failure.

records.title: Stretched/Worn Timing Chain on 3.6L V6
records.howToFix: Replace the timing chains, guides, and tensioners (a full front-of-engine job). If covered under GM Special Coverage #11340C the repair is free up to 10yr/120k mi; otherwise it is an out-of-pocket repair. Keeping oil changes current and using correct-spec oil slows wear.
records.repairItems: Complete timing chains, guides and tensioners; Special Coverage 11340C check; correct oil
destinations: complete kit for verified year/engine split
records.reason: The ACDelco kit is verified for 2009-2013 LLT/VIN D. The 2008 LY7 application is different and remains held.
records.correction: Split 2008 LY7 from 2009-2013 LLT. Flag as overlapping/duplicative with buick-enclave-timing-chain-2008-2012.

records.ymmt: 2008-2012 | Buick | Enclave | CX, CXL, CXL-1, CXL-2, Premium | 3.6L LLT V6
records.title: Enclave 3.6L LLT Timing Chain Stretch + Oil Consumption
records.howToFix: Timing chain replacement ($2,500-$4,500 with 3-row crossover labor premium). Walnut-blast intake valve carbon at the same time ($300-$500). PCV system update per TSB. Some owners refuse the chain job at this mileage and trade — failure can mean total engine replacement ($6,000+).
records.repairItems: Timing-chain repair; intake-valve walnut blast; PCV update; possible engine replacement
records.reason: The product covers only the timing-chain portion. Walnut blasting and PCV updates are separate services, and 2008 is not an LLT application.
records.correction: Correct the 2008 engine designation (LY7, not LLT), hold its part link, and consolidate this duplicate with the broader timing-chain issue.

records.title: Torque Converter Clutch (TCC) Shudder
records.howToFix: Per GM bulletin: flush and refill with the specified DEXRON-VI fluid (part 88862156) and reprogram the TCM with a fast-learn relearn. Persistent cases may require torque converter replacement.
records.repairItems: DEXRON-VI fluid exchange; TCM reprogram and fast-learn; possible torque converter
destinations: ACDelco GM OE DEXRON-VI full-synthetic ATF, 1 gallon, 88865618
2014-2020 Enclave; confirm transmission and bulletin procedure
records.reason: The fluid is verified for the full issue span. TCM programming/fast-learn and converter diagnosis are shop procedures, not replaced by the fluid link.
records.correction: Update obsolete/bulk part 88862156 to current retail GM package 88865618 while retaining the DEXRON-VI specification.

records.title: Water Pump Leak / Coolant Loss on 3.6L V6
records.howToFix: Replace the water pump (and thermostat/gasket as needed), then refill and bleed the cooling system. A relatively common, moderate-cost repair on these vehicles.
records.repairItems: Water pump and gasket; thermostat/gasket if diagnosed; coolant refill and bleed
destinations: GM Genuine water-pump kit with gasket 12709178
2008-2017 Enclave issue scope; GM catalog includes these years
records.reason: The GM product is an exact water-pump-with-gasket repair part for the issue span. Thermostat replacement remains conditional.
records.correction: Keep thermostat/gasket as 'as needed' and include the cooling-system bleed step; do not imply the pump covers every coolant leak.

records.ymmt: 2013-2022 | Buick | Encore | Base, Convenience, Leather, Premium, Sport Touring, Preferred, Essence | 1.4L Turbo LUJ/LUV
records.title: Encore 1.4L Turbo (LUJ/LUV) Timing Chain Stretch
records.howToFix: Full chain kit including chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets ($1,200-$2,000). Use dexos1 full-synthetic 5W-30 and stick to 5,000-mile intervals — extended OLM intervals are the dominant cause. Catastrophic chain skip means head rebuild ($3,500+).
records.repairItems: Timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets; dexos1 5W-30 maintenance
records.reason: The kit has verified 2013-2021 1.4L fitment; the issue's 2022 model year remains unverified for this exact product.
records.correction: Hold 2022 rather than stretching the product fitment. Confirm kit contents before claiming every sprocket/guide is included.

records.title: 6T40 Automatic Transmission Hard Shifting, Shudder and Slipping
records.howToFix: Service the transmission with the correct fluid; for shudder, a torque-converter clutch fluid/flush or solenoid replacement may help. Persistent 2-6 slip/flare typically requires valve body/channel-plate cleaning or rebuild. Confirm GM software calibration is current, as updated shift logic addressed some complaints.
records.repairItems: Correct DEXRON-VI fluid service; possible TCC/solenoid; valve body/channel plate; rebuild; software calibration
destinations: ACDelco GM OE DEXRON-VI ATF, 1 quart, 88865601
2013-2018 Encore issue scope; official catalog lists 2013-2022
records.reason: DEXRON-VI is verified, but the remaining fixes depend on whether the fault is converter, solenoid/TEHCM, valve body, calibration, or internal damage.
records.correction: Do not link a solenoid, TEHCM, scanner, or rebuild kit until diagnosis identifies that repair. The fluid link is not a promise that service cures slipping.

records.title: Encore GX (2020+) Three-Cylinder Turbo Stalling and Low-Oil-Pressure ECM Recall
records.howToFix: Have the ECM reprogrammed under the GM recall to ensure low-oil-pressure conditions (P0521) are properly flagged. Diagnose stalling/power-loss with a scan tool. Monitor oil level frequently given the small-displacement turbo's sensitivity to low oil.
records.repairItems: ECM recall calibration; scan-tool diagnosis if the recall does not resolve the condition; verify oil level/pressure
records.reason: The repair begins with an ECM calibration and VIN eligibility, not a timing, oil-pump, or scanner purchase.
records.correction: The title says Encore/Encore GX, but the three-cylinder application is Encore GX. Replace the unrelated purge-valve citation before publication.

records.title: Encore GX Transmission Shudder, Jerking and Solenoid Faults
records.howToFix: Diagnose with a scan tool for solenoid and torque-converter fault codes. Repairs range from shift-solenoid replacement and a torque-converter clutch service to torque converter or full transmission replacement in severe cases. Check for applicable GM service bulletins and lemon-law/warranty coverage on repeat failures.
records.repairItems: Transmission-capable diagnosis; software; solenoid/valve body, torque converter or transmission only after fault isolation
destinations: 2020-2023 Encore GX; transmission identification and module diagnosis required
records.reason: The How to Fix names several mutually exclusive repairs. A generic OBD scanner or single transmission part would be misleading.
records.correction: Replace the unrelated charge-air-cooler citation and keep commerce gated by transmission ID and diagnosis.

records.title: Engine Stalling and Sudden Power Loss While Driving (Early Models)
records.howToFix: Diagnose with a scan tool to isolate the trigger (camshaft/crankshaft position sensors, throttle body, turbo underboost, or misfire). Common repairs include throttle body replacement, sensor replacement, and addressing the turbo/PCV issues above. Apply current GM software updates, as some driveability concerns were addressed via ECM reprogramming.
records.repairItems: Scan-tool and fuel/air diagnosis; repair the confirmed sensor, throttle-body, turbo, PCV or calibration fault
records.reason: The symptom has multiple unrelated causes and the repair text explicitly requires diagnosis.
records.correction: Do not generate an OBD or throttle-body CTA from the error codes alone.

records.title: EVAP Purge Pump Failure (2022 Encore) - Warranty Extension
records.howToFix: Replace the EVAP purge pump under GM's special coverage / warranty extension (up to 15 yr / 150,000 mi). Owners who already paid out of pocket may be eligible for reimbursement. Confirm exact eligibility and codes with a GM dealer.
records.repairItems: VIN eligibility and dealer replacement of the EVAP purge pump under special coverage
records.reason: The stated repair is a covered purge-pump replacement. The coverage check should precede any purchase.
records.correction: Keep the CTA on official VIN coverage rather than a generic purge valve.

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption (1.4L Turbo)
records.howToFix: Check oil level frequently between changes and top off as needed. Diagnose and repair the PCV/camshaft cover system, which is a common contributor. Perform a documented oil-consumption test at a dealer; persistent high consumption may require valve cover, PCV, or piston ring/seal service.
records.repairItems: Oil-consumption test; PCV/cam cover if confirmed; intake/check valve or piston-ring repair only when diagnosed
destinations: 2013-2021 Encore 1.4L except LE2; only after PCV/cam-cover diagnosis
records.reason: The live product includes the gasket and bolts and lists 2013+ Encore excluding LE2, but it does not address intake check-valve or ring failure.
records.correction: Show the valve cover only after diagnosis; keep ring/short-block work as service-only.

records.ymmt: 2020-2024 | Buick | Encore GX | Preferred, Select, Essence, Sport Touring, Avenir | 1.2L Turbo, 1.3L Turbo
records.title: Encore GX CVT / 9-Speed Hesitation and Shudder
records.howToFix: CVT: software update via dealer (TSB 21-NA-141 and successors). 9-speed: ATF flush + reprogramming if persistent shudder; valve body or torque converter if not resolved. Many fixes were under GM's "PI" (Product Investigation) bulletins — check for active campaigns on your VIN.
records.repairItems: Identify CVT versus 9-speed; calibration/fast learn; transmission-specific fluid; valve body or converter only if diagnosed
records.reason: The CVT and 9-speed use different procedures and fluids. A shared fluid or solenoid link would be unsafe.
records.correction: Replace the unrelated turbo-coverage citations and split the repair by transmission before adding parts.

records.title: ECM Ignition Timing Fault Causing Engine Knock After Auto Stop/Start (Recall A242435780)
records.howToFix: Covered under GM recall A242435780 (NHTSA 11006392) - the dealer reprograms the engine control module free of charge (no parts required). Owners noticing knock or a check engine light after stop/start cycles should have the ECM reflashed promptly to avoid engine damage.
records.repairItems: Recall ECM reprogramming
records.reason: The remedy is software only; no retail part or scanner purchase is called for.
records.correction: Use the official VIN/recall route.

records.title: Electronic Brake Boost Sensor Connection Failure - Loss of Power Assist (Recall 20V588)
records.howToFix: Covered under NHTSA recall 20V588 (GM A202307262) - the dealer replaces the electronic brake boost module free of charge. Owners with a hard brake pedal or brake-assist warning should verify recall completion via VIN at nhtsa.gov and have the module replaced.
records.repairItems: Recall inspection and dealer replacement of the electronic brake-boost module as directed
records.reason: This is a safety-recall remedy with VIN-controlled parts and procedures.
records.correction: Do not place a brake-booster purchase ahead of the recall repair.

records.title: False "Shift to Park" Warning / Park Switch Failure (TSB 23-NA-119)
records.howToFix: Per GM TSB 23-NA-119, the fix is inspecting the park-switch terminals and, if no harness damage is found, replacing the shifter control assembly. Confirm a clean shutdown afterward to prevent parasitic battery drain. Repair may be covered under bumper-to-bumper warranty.
records.repairItems: Inspect shifter terminals/harness; replace shifter control only if terminals are undamaged and the bulletin directs replacement
destinations: 2020-2023 Encore GX; inspect connector before parts
records.reason: The shifter is conditional; harness or terminal damage changes the repair.
records.correction: Do not link a shifter assembly until VIN and connector condition establish the correct part.

records.title: Incorrect Catalytic Converter Installed at Factory (Emissions Recall A202317281)
records.howToFix: Covered under GM emissions recall A202317281 (NHTSA 10197318) - dealers inspect the catalytic converter and replace it with the correct part (e.g. P/N 55515139) at no charge if the wrong unit was installed. Verify eligibility by VIN at nhtsa.gov.
records.repairItems: Emission-recall inspection and VIN-specific catalytic-converter replacement
records.reason: The recall supplies the correct converter by VIN; a retail converter risks the wrong emissions calibration.
records.correction: Verify the published year span because the cited campaigns cover specific 2020-2021 and 2023 populations rather than every 2020-2023 vehicle.

records.title: Instrument Panel Display Goes Blank While Driving (Recall 23V744 - VCU Software)
records.howToFix: Covered under NHTSA recall 23V744 (GM A232424320) - the VCU software is updated by a dealer or via over-the-air (OTA) update free of charge. Owners experiencing a blank cluster should confirm the recall is applied and that their software is current.
records.repairItems: Recall VCU software update by dealer or approved OTA process
records.reason: The remedy is software, not an instrument-cluster or scanner purchase.
records.correction: Route users to the official recall workflow.

records.title: PCV / Camshaft Cover Diaphragm Failure (1.4L Turbo) - "Tea Kettle" Whistle
records.howToFix: Replace the camshaft (valve) cover, which contains the integrated PCV diaphragm; many owners upgrade to a revised cover. The root-cause check valve in the intake manifold should also be addressed (replace manifold or install an external check-valve/PCV bypass kit) to prevent turbo boost from over-pressurizing the crankcase. Check eligibility under GM Special Coverage N202299080.
records.repairItems: Integrated PCV camshaft cover; inspect intake-manifold check valve; coverage eligibility
destinations: 2013-2021 Encore 1.4L except LE2; cover, gasket and bolts
records.reason: The live page explicitly includes the valve cover gasket/bolts and Encore fitment. Intake-manifold check-valve damage remains a separate diagnosis.
records.correction: Do not call the cover a complete repair when the intake check valve has also failed.

records.title: Turbocharger / Oil Supply Line Failure Causing Sudden Loss of Power
records.howToFix: Replace the turbocharger assembly along with the turbo oil feed pipe seals, oil return pipe gaskets, exhaust/coolant seals, and related hardware per GM's procedure. For 2017-2018 models, check eligibility for the GM turbocharger warranty extension (10 yr / 120,000 mi). Maintain strict oil change intervals to avoid oil-feed line coking that accelerates turbo failure.
records.repairItems: Turbocharger assembly; new oil feed/return lines; seals, gaskets and hardware; coverage check
records.reason: The OEM page verifies the turbo assembly and instructs replacement of feed/return lines, which are not included in the single link.
records.correction: Label this partial and list lines/seals/hardware separately after VIN lookup.

records.title: Top-End Engine Ticking from Hydraulic Lash Adjusters (LSY 2.0T)
records.howToFix: Per PIP6101A, dealer removes camshaft carrier, inspects for soft SHLAs, and replaces failed lash adjusters AND their matched rocker arms. Covered under powertrain warranty - do not let dealer dismiss as normal direct-injection noise.
records.repairItems: Dealer inspection; matched lash adjusters and rocker arms only for confirmed affected positions
records.reason: Part count and positions are determined during inspection and the repair is within the powertrain-warranty context.
records.correction: Do not sell a generic lifter set before inspection.

records.title: 3.6L V6 Timing Chain Stretch and Wear
records.howToFix: Replace the timing chains, guides, and tensioners (a full timing set) along with the cam phasers; budget for a labor-intensive front-of-engine teardown. Maintain strict 5,000-mile oil changes with the correct dexos1 oil to prevent recurrence. GM revised chain and tensioner components for later production engines.
records.repairItems: Complete timing chains, guides and tensioners; inspect cam phasers; correct dexos1 oil
records.reason: The live page is in stock, offers Add to Cart and lists 2010-2012 LaCrosse; the GM bulletin covers high-feature V6 chain kits, but cam phasers may be separate.
records.correction: Replace the unrelated ignition-recall citation and require RPO/VIN confirmation.

records.title: 3.8L V6 Lower Intake Manifold Gasket / Plastic Coolant Elbow Leaks
records.howToFix: Replace the lower intake manifold gaskets with GM's revised gasket (higher-temp rubber with metal coolant-passage inserts) and swap the plastic coolant elbows for metal Dorman replacements. Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect for oil/coolant intermixing during the repair.
records.repairItems: Revised lower-intake gasket set; aluminum coolant elbows; coolant refill and contamination inspection
destinations: GM 3.8L application; confirm both elbow shapes before purchase
records.reason: The gasket set is listed for the 2009 LaCrosse and the metal elbows address the failure named in How to Fix.
records.correction: Keep the engine/VIN check visible and do not substitute the similarly numbered MS98003T.

records.ymmt: 2010-2016 | Buick | LaCrosse | CX, CXL, CXS, Touring, Premium I, Premium II, Premium III, Sport Touring | 3.6L LFX/LLT V6
records.title: LaCrosse 3.6L LLT/LFX Timing Chain Stretch
records.howToFix: Full timing chain kit ($2,000-$3,500 incl. labor) — both primary and secondary chains, all tensioners and guides. Switch to 5,000-7,500 mile oil intervals with full-synthetic dexos1 5W-30. LLT engines may also need PCV valve replacement to reduce oil consumption (TSB 10-06-01-007).
records.repairItems: Complete timing chains, guides and tensioners; oil service; LLT PCV update when applicable
records.reason: The linked kit is verified for the early high-feature V6 application; the 2013-2016 LFX span needs its own exact kit.
records.correction: Split LLT and LFX years instead of stretching one product across 2010-2016.

records.title: Driver Door Wiring Splice Corrosion (Recall 14V317000)
records.howToFix: Under recall 14V317000, dealers inspect the driver door window motor harness and replace the electrical splice as necessary, free of charge. For non-recall door-harness wear, repair or re-splice the broken wires in the door jamb flex loom.
records.repairItems: Recall inspection/replacement of the door-harness splice; harness repair only as directed
records.reason: The repair depends on inspected corrosion extent and recall eligibility.
records.correction: Do not sell a universal wiring pigtail as the complete repair.

records.title: eAssist 12V Battery Drain and "Service Battery Charging System" Warnings
records.howToFix: Have the dealer diagnose the Generator Control Module and Battery Energy Control Module per the GM exchange/recall program; replace failed modules and the 12V battery as needed. Check for the open recall by VIN. Inspect the hybrid battery control module wiring harness for shorts when chasing parasitic drain.
records.repairItems: Hybrid-system diagnosis; 12V battery, module or hybrid harness only when confirmed; recall/VIN check
records.reason: Battery drain can originate in the battery, modules or hybrid harness, so a battery link alone would be incomplete.
records.correction: Require eAssist-capable diagnosis before parts.

records.title: Electronic Power Steering Connector Corrosion / Loss of Assist (Recall 17V116000)
records.howToFix: Under recall 17V116000, dealers inspect, correct the seal seating, and secure the EPS connector seals free of charge. Owners should verify the recall has been completed by VIN; if assist is lost, have the EPS connectors and module inspected for corrosion.
records.repairItems: Recall inspection and sealing/repair of the EPS connector
records.reason: The remedy is VIN-controlled and connector-condition dependent.
records.correction: Do not infer that the steering gear must be replaced.

records.title: HVAC Blower Motor and Climate Control Module Failures
records.howToFix: Replace the failed blower motor (and resistor module on older cars) as a common wear repair. For frozen climate controls, update or replace the ECC/HVAC control module per GM software updates; inspect connectors for corrosion.
records.repairItems: Diagnose blower circuit; older blower motor/resistor; later ECC/HVAC module or software; inspect connectors
destinations: 2008 LaCrosse; select exact resistor/control module after connector and HVAC-option check
records.reason: The product category is live and year-filtered, but automatic-climate modules and resistor types differ across 2008-2014.
records.correction: Split 2008-2009 hardware from later module/software cases; do not show one resistor for every year.

records.title: Intermittent Low-Beam Headlight Failure
records.howToFix: Diagnose the headlight wiring, the underhood bussed electrical center/relays, and the headlamp switch/connectors for heat damage and loose terminals; repair or replace affected harness connectors and relays. Some owners resolve it by replacing corroded headlamp socket connectors.
records.repairItems: Electrical diagnosis of harness, fuse block, relay/driver, switch, connector or lamp socket
records.reason: The How to Fix names several non-interchangeable causes; no single bulb, relay or harness is justified.
records.correction: Do not link headlight bulbs when the known issue is an intermittent control-circuit failure.

records.title: Rear Suspension Toe-Link May Loosen / Fracture (Recalls 17V267000 & later)
records.howToFix: Under the applicable recall, dealers inspect the left and right rear suspension toe-link assemblies and correct the installation or replace corroded links free of charge. Owners in road-salt states should check for the expanded toe-link recall by VIN and have rear suspension inspected.
records.repairItems: Recall inspection/replacement of rear toe links and required fasteners; alignment
records.reason: Recall parts and alignment procedure are VIN-controlled.
records.correction: Keep retail suspension links behind the recall check.

records.title: Electronic Climate Control Programmer / Blower Control Module Failure
records.howToFix: Diagnose by powering the blower motor directly; if the motor runs, replace the blower control module (mounted near the blower under the dash or cowl) or the HVAC programmer on earlier cars. Aftermarket modules are inexpensive, and replacement restores normal automatic fan operation.
records.repairItems: Direct blower test; blower-control module on later cars or HVAC programmer on earlier cars
destinations: 2000-2005 LeSabre 3.8L sedan; only after direct blower/circuit test
records.reason: The live page is in stock with Add to Cart, lists 2000-2005 LeSabre 3.8L and cross-references OEM 52480042; 1992-1999 uses other programmers/modules.
records.correction: Split the 1992-1999 applications and require automatic-climate option confirmation.

records.title: Front Strut Mount and Bearing Wear — Clunking and Popping Over Bumps and in Turns
records.howToFix: Replace both front strut mounts; most shops install complete loaded strut assemblies (quick-struts) in pairs since the struts themselves are usually tired at the same mileage. An alignment afterward is recommended.
records.repairItems: Both front strut mounts/bearings or paired loaded struts; alignment
destinations: Monroe Strut-Mate 902972 front strut mount kit
records.reason: The live page is in stock with Add to Cart and its fitment table lists 2000-2005 LeSabre front. Replace both sides and align afterward.
records.correction: State that alignment and paired replacement remain required service steps.

records.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator Diaphragm Leak — Fire Risk Recall (NHTSA 04V090000 / GM 03054B)
records.howToFix: GM dealers replaced the regulator with a revised design free of charge under recall 03054B; check the VIN for open recall completion. If the recall was never performed or the replacement has since failed, install a new fuel pressure regulator — an inexpensive job since the regulator sits on top of the fuel rail.
records.repairItems: Recall/VIN check and revised fuel-pressure regulator if directed
records.reason: A fuel-leak/fire-risk campaign should route to the recall before a regulator purchase.
records.correction: Do not bypass the recall with a generic regulator.

records.title: PASS-Key Anti-Theft System Fault — Security Light On, Engine Cranks but Won't Start
records.howToFix: Try the relearn/wait procedure (key on with security light flashing for about 10 minutes, then restart) to get going. The lasting fix is replacing the ignition lock cylinder/Passkey sensor (and worn keys) followed by the security relearn; some owners on older resistor-pellet cars install a matched bypass resistor instead.
records.repairItems: Pass-Key diagnosis/relearn; ignition lock cylinder/sensor and keys only when confirmed
destinations: 1992-2005 LeSabre; theft-system generation and key code required
records.reason: The repair differs by Pass-Key generation and may be a relearn rather than hardware.
records.correction: Do not promote resistor bypasses or a lock cylinder without diagnosing the exact system.

records.title: Plastic Upper Intake Manifold (Plenum) Degradation Causing Coolant Leak and Hydro-Lock Risk
records.howToFix: Replace the upper intake manifold with the revised GM service kit or an improved aftermarket plenum (with updated gaskets and EGR stovepipe), per GM TSB 04-06-01-017. Most shops replace the lower intake gaskets at the same time since the manifold is already off. Never keep driving with unexplained coolant loss — internal leaks can hydro-lock the engine.
records.repairItems: Revised upper intake plenum with gaskets/EGR stovepipe; inspect lower-intake gaskets
destinations: Dorman 615-180 upper intake manifold with gaskets
records.reason: The live product is in stock and includes the intake manifold, gaskets and PCV items; Dorman lists Buick 1995-2005 applications.
records.correction: Keep lower-intake gasket replacement conditional on inspection.

records.title: Power Window Regulator Cable Failure (Windows Drop or Stop Working)
records.howToFix: Replace the failed window regulator assembly with an updated aftermarket unit (commonly available for $50-$100); the motor can usually be reused. Many owners replace regulators in remaining doors preemptively or keep a spare, since failures across all four windows are widely reported.
records.repairItems: Position-specific window regulator assembly; reuse motor only if it tests good
destinations: 2000-2005 LeSabre; select front/rear and driver/passenger position
records.reason: The live catalog lists exact OEM regulators and position labels for the issue span.
records.correction: Require door position before purchase and do not imply the motor is always included or failed.

records.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump and Fuel Level Sender Failure (Stalling, No-Start, Erratic Gauge)
records.howToFix: Replace the complete fuel pump module assembly (pump, sender, and strainer together) — the tank must be dropped on these cars. Replacing the whole module rather than just the pump fixes the erratic fuel gauge at the same time.
records.repairItems: Fuel-pressure/electrical diagnosis; complete pump module/sender/strainer for the exact year and tank configuration
records.reason: The 2004-2005 OEM module 19369903 is verified, but earlier years use different modules.
records.correction: Do not stretch 19369903 across 1998-2003; force year/VIN selection.

records.title: Fuel Pump Relay Overheats and Melts Fuse Box (Crank/No-Start, Stalling)
records.howToFix: Repair the melted fuse box terminal/relay socket and replace the fuel pump relay; severe cases require replacing the fuse box. Inspecting and re-terminating the relay circuit (rather than just swapping the pump) is the correct fix. Some owners relocate/upgrade the relay terminal to prevent recurrence.
records.repairItems: Inspect relay, terminals and underhood fuse block; repair/relocate socket or replace fuse block based on heat damage
destinations: 2008-2011 Lucerne; inspect heat damage before parts
records.reason: A new relay alone is unsafe if the terminal or fuse block is heat-damaged.
records.correction: Gate every part behind a terminal/fuse-block inspection.

records.title: Heated Windshield Washer Fluid Module Fire Risk (Microheat)
records.howToFix: Covered under NHTSA recalls 08V441000 (first remedy) and 10V240000 (second/final remedy). Dealers permanently disable and remove the heated washer module and reroute the washer fluid hoses. GM paid affected owners $100 each.
records.repairItems: Recall removal/disablement of the heated-washer module and hose reroute
records.reason: The recall remedy removes/disables the module; buying another heated module contradicts the repair.
records.correction: No retail module CTA.

records.title: Ignition Switch Can Slip Out of Run Position
records.howToFix: Covered under NHTSA recall 14V355000 (part of GM's large 2014 ignition-switch campaign). Dealers inspect/replace the ignition key/switch components. As an interim measure GM advised drivers to use only the ignition key with nothing else on the ring until the remedy was performed.
records.repairItems: Recall inspection and key/switch remedy as directed by VIN
records.reason: The safety campaign controls whether the key, switch or both are serviced.
records.correction: Do not sell an ignition switch before the VIN recall check.

records.title: Instrument Cluster Hard to Read in Daylight
records.howToFix: GM's remedy is replacement of the instrument panel cluster (IPC) with a revised version that has larger, higher-contrast numerals. The replacement is easier to read in daylight, though it still does not fully illuminate during the day.
records.repairItems: Diagnose brightness/power; revised instrument cluster when confirmed; VIN programming
records.reason: A replacement IPC must match options/mileage and be programmed; a bare cluster is not plug-and-play.
records.correction: Use a service route rather than an unprogrammed module purchase.

records.title: Intermediate Steering Shaft Clunk During Slow Turns
records.howToFix: GM TSB 06-02-35-009H covers this. Early remedy was to lubricate/realign the cardan joint; the durable fix is replacing the intermediate steering shaft with the updated design (GM P/N 25810450). The TSB explicitly advises against replacing the steering rack for this noise.
records.repairItems: Inspect/lubricate/realign intermediate shaft; replace with updated shaft if needed
destinations: 2006-2009 Lucerne; confirm shaft rather than rack
records.reason: GM 25810450 has exact Lucerne fitment but is discontinued on the verified page; lubrication/realignment may solve the issue.
records.correction: Do not present a discontinued shaft as buyable or replace the steering rack for this symptom.

records.title: Northstar 4.6L V8 Head Gasket / Head Bolt Thread Failure
records.howToFix: Proper repair requires removing the heads and installing oversized thread inserts (e.g., a head-stud/Time-Sert kit) before fitting new head gaskets. This is labor-intensive (engine often pulled), so repair bills commonly run several thousand dollars; some owners replace the engine instead.
records.repairItems: Northstar specialist diagnosis; oversized block-thread inserts/Time-Sert process; head gaskets and machine inspection
records.reason: Correct insert size, tooling and machine condition cannot be established from YMMT alone.
records.correction: Do not link sealers or a head-gasket-only kit as the fix.

records.ymmt: 2006-2011 | Buick | Lucerne | CXS, Super, Special Edition | 4.6L L37 Northstar V8
records.title: Lucerne Northstar V8 Head Bolt Pull / Coolant Loss
records.howToFix: Northstar "time-sert" head bolt repair is the durable fix — block must be removed (engine out or in some cases above-engine work), threads drilled out, larger steel inserts installed. $3,500-$6,000 specialist labor. Some owners try "Block-Tite" / sealants as a band-aid; not durable. Watch coolant level monthly.
records.repairItems: Oversized block-thread inserts with head gaskets; specialist inspection of block and heads
records.reason: This duplicates the broader Northstar head-gasket/head-bolt issue and cannot be safely reduced to one retail kit.
records.correction: Consolidate the duplicate and explicitly reject cooling-system sealants.

records.title: Rear Air Self-Leveling Suspension Failure (Sagging Rear)
records.howToFix: Diagnose the specific failure point: replace leaking air shocks, the height sensor, or the air compressor (the relief valve is integral to the compressor, so a stuck valve means a full compressor replacement). Some owners convert to conventional non-air shocks/coils to eliminate the system.
records.repairItems: Diagnose rear shocks, height sensor and compressor; repair failed component or convert to passive shocks
records.reason: Monroe explicitly covers 2006-2010 Lucerne; 2011 remains outside the verified kit span, and component repair may be preferable.
records.correction: Hold 2011 and label conversion as an option, not proof that the compressor or shocks failed.

records.title: Throttle Body / Throttle Position Sensor Causing Reduced Engine Power
records.howToFix: Clean the throttle body first; if the TPS/electronic throttle body has failed, replace it and perform the required throttle relearn so the computer sets correct idle and full-throttle positions. GM Special Coverage extended this to 10 years / 120,000 miles on covered 2009-2011 models.
records.repairItems: Throttle-body diagnosis/cleaning; engine-specific throttle body if confirmed; electronic relearn
records.reason: The catalog exposes three different throttle bodies by engine/year and live buyable listings.
records.correction: Require engine/VIN selection and relearn; do not imply one throttle body fits every Lucerne.

records.ymmt: 2011-2017 | Buick | Regal | GS, Premium, Turbo, Sport Touring | 2.0L Turbo LHU, 2.0L Turbo LTG
records.title: Regal 2.0L Turbo (LHU/LTG) Timing Chain Stretch
records.howToFix: Full timing chain kit including chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets — $1,800-$3,000 at independent. Stick to 5,000-7,500 mile oil intervals with dexos1 full-synthetic 5W-30. Carbon-clean intake valves at the same service ($300-$500) since LHU/LTG are direct-injection.
records.repairItems: Complete engine-specific timing kit; inspect valves; intake-valve cleaning; correct oil
destinations: 2011-2013 Regal 2.0L, including VIN V where listed; verify engine/VIN
records.reason: The live product lists 2011-2013 2.0L fitment and kit contents. LHU and LTG are different applications, so 2014-2017 needs a separate product.
records.correction: Split LHU from LTG and do not call walnut blasting part of a timing kit.

records.title: 6T70/6T40 Automatic Transmission Shudder, Slipping & Hard Shifts
records.howToFix: Start with a full transmission fluid/filter service (fixes many shudder cases). Persistent problems require valve body cleaning/rebuild, accumulator bore repair, or torque converter replacement. Use only the correct GM spec fluid.
records.repairItems: Identify transmission; correct DEXRON-VI fluid/filter service; valve body, accumulator or converter only after diagnosis
destinations: 2011-2017 Regal with transmission requiring DEXRON-VI; verify unit and capacity
records.reason: The fluid is appropriate only after confirming a 6T-series unit; hard parts differ between 6T40/6T70 and failure mode.
records.correction: Do not merge 6T40 and 6T70 repair parts or imply a fluid service cures internal slipping.

records.ymmt: 2011-2017 | Buick | Regal | CXL, GS, Premium, Turbo | 2.0L Turbo, 2.4L, 3.6L V6
records.title: Regal Aisin AF40 6-Speed Harsh Shifts / Shudder
records.howToFix: Drain-and-fill ATF every 50,000 miles using AC Delco / Aisin AFW+ (or JWS3309 equivalent) — about $150-$250 DIY (5-6 qt drained per service). Severe shudder may need torque converter or valve body work ($1,500-$3,500). If neglected past 120k miles, full rebuild may be required ($3,500-$5,500).
records.repairItems: GM AW/Aisin Warner fluid service; diagnose valve body/solenoids/internal wear; software as applicable
destinations: ACDelco GM OE AW transmission fluid 19256039
2011-2013 Regal GS listed by Buick; confirm AF40/VIN
records.reason: Buick's official product page lists GM AW fluid 19256039 for 2011-2013 Regal GS. The current JWS 3309 claim is not supported for this application.
records.correction: Replace JWS 3309/Aisin AFW+ language with GM AW-1 specification and narrow the year/trim scope to verified AF40 applications.

records.title: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves (Direct Injection)
records.howToFix: Perform a walnut-blasting / manual intake valve cleaning (or chemical induction service in milder cases). Updated engine-management software and periodic intake cleaning help slow recurrence; catch-can installation reduces future buildup.
records.repairItems: Borescope/airflow diagnosis; walnut-shell or manual intake-valve cleaning; optional catch can is not the repair
records.reason: The specified remedy is a cleaning service, not an OBD scanner or replacement intake part.
records.correction: Do not market a catch can as a cure for existing deposits.

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption on 2.4L Ecotec
records.howToFix: GM TSB diagnostic involves an oil consumption test; remedies range from PCV/valve cover updates to piston and ring replacement. Owners commonly manage it by checking oil frequently and topping off, or rebuilding the short block in severe cases.
records.repairItems: Oil-consumption test; PCV/cam cover if confirmed; piston/ring or short-block repair only after diagnosis
records.reason: The possible repairs range from a cover to internal engine work, so no single retail part is justified.
records.correction: Keep the CTA on diagnosis and coverage before parts.

records.title: Loss of Power Brake Assist — EBCM Software Defect (Recall)
records.howToFix: Dealers reprogram/update the EBCM software at no cost; no replacement parts required. Owners should verify the recall has been completed via VIN.
records.repairItems: Recall EBCM software update
records.reason: The remedy is software and safety-critical.
records.correction: Do not link a brake booster, sensor or scanner.

records.title: Rear Suspension Toe Link Corrosion / Fracture (Salt-Belt Recall)
records.howToFix: Under recall, dealers replace the rear suspension toe links and adjuster fasteners at no cost. Out of recall scope, replace corroded toe links with new parts.
records.repairItems: Recall replacement of rear toe links/fasteners and alignment
records.reason: The campaign remedy and parts are VIN-controlled.
records.correction: Recall check precedes any retail suspension link.

records.title: Sudden Loss of Electric Power Steering Assist (Recall)
records.howToFix: Under recall 21510, dealers replace the electric belt-drive rack-and-pinion steering gear assembly free of charge. Non-recall failures require diagnosis of the steering rack motor/module and replacement.
records.repairItems: Recall replacement of the electric steering gear as directed by VIN
records.reason: Steering gear replacement is a safety-recall procedure with VIN-specific configuration.
records.correction: Do not sell an unprogrammed steering gear.

records.title: Timing Chain / Tensioner Failure on 2.0T Turbo (LHU/LNF)
records.howToFix: Replace the timing chain, tensioner, guides and any damaged valvetrain components; severe cases require partial or full engine rebuild. Preventively, change oil more frequently (~5,000 miles) and address any P0008/P0016/P0017 codes immediately before the chain jumps time.
records.repairItems: Complete chain, tensioner and guides; inspect valve/piston damage; correct oil
records.reason: The live listing covers the stated early 2.0L span and enumerates timing components, but internal damage is not covered.
records.correction: Consolidate with the broader Regal 2.0T timing-chain entry and keep post-failure engine inspection explicit.

records.ymmt: 1994-1996 | Buick | Roadmaster | Roadmaster Sedan, Roadmaster Estate Wagon, Roadmaster Limited | 5.7L LT1 V8 (Gen II)
records.title: 4L60E automatic transmission wear (valve body, sprag, harsh shift/no downshift)
records.howToFix: For early valve-body symptoms, a valve body rebuild/updated valves and a fluid/filter service may suffice. For slipping or sprag/clutch failure, a full rebuild with upgraded hard parts (sunshell, sprag) is the accepted fix.
records.repairItems: Transmission diagnosis; valve-body service or rebuild with upgraded sunshell/sprag and damaged hard parts
destinations: 1993-1996 4L60E super-master rebuild kit with HD sunshell
1994-1996 Roadmaster 4L60E; transmission builder must confirm year-specific unit
records.reason: The kit is year-correct and includes the named HD sunshell, but rebuild contents must follow teardown and the transmission's year-specific calibration.
records.correction: Route to a transmission specialist and do not imply the kit covers every failed hard part or converter.

records.ymmt: 1994-1996 | Buick | Roadmaster | Roadmaster Sedan, Roadmaster Estate Wagon, Roadmaster Limited | 5.7L LT1 V8 (Gen II)
records.title: ABS hydraulic modulator corrosion / front brake fluid leak (safety recall)
records.howToFix: Have the ABS modulator inspected and, if corroded/leaking, replaced (the recall remedy). Verify recall completion by VIN. Out-of-warranty, the modulator can be replaced with a known-good used or rebuilt unit and the system bled.
records.repairItems: Safety-recall inspection/replacement of ABS hydraulic modulator; rebuilt/used sourcing only if no coverage
records.reason: A leaking hydraulic modulator is safety-critical and the original remedy is recall-controlled; used units need specialist inspection.
records.correction: Do not direct users to a used modulator before the VIN recall check.

records.title: Estate Wagon Rear Self-Leveling Air Shock and Compressor Failure
records.howToFix: Diagnose first: inspect the height sensor wiring under the driver-side rear seat for broken/corroded wires, test the sensor, and check the air lines for leaks at the shock fittings. If the shocks themselves leak, the most common modern fix is a conversion kit (Strutmasters CADR3 or similar) that replaces the air shocks with passive gas shocks and either deletes the air system or splits compressor output to aftermarket air bags via a T-fitting. Replace the compressor relay or compressor if it sticks on. Many owners simply unplug the compressor and run conventional shocks to eliminate the system entirely.
records.repairItems: Diagnose compressor, height sensor and air shocks; repair failed component or install wagon conversion kit
destinations: Strutmasters CADR3 rear air-shock conversion kit
records.reason: The live page explicitly lists the wagon, full year span, two coil-over shocks and required hardware.
records.correction: Keep diagnosis first and do not apply the wagon kit to sedans.

records.ymmt: 1994-1996 | Buick | Roadmaster | Roadmaster Sedan, Roadmaster Estate Wagon, Roadmaster Limited | 5.7L LT1 V8 (Gen II)
records.title: Fuel pump / in-tank check valve failure causing hard starting and low pressure
records.howToFix: Verify fuel pressure with a gauge (prime and leak-down test) before condemning the pump. Replace the in-tank fuel pump/sending-unit module (check valve is integral); inspect the pressure relief valve. The sending unit shares the module, so a weak float/gauge reading often accompanies pump wear.
records.repairItems: Fuel-pressure/leak-down diagnosis; complete fuel-pump module/sending unit when check valve or pump is confirmed
records.reason: The product page states the exact 1994-1996 5.7L Roadmaster application; a pressure test is still required because injectors/regulator can also lose pressure.
records.correction: Do not link a pump from the hard-start symptom alone.

records.ymmt: 1994-1996 | Buick | Roadmaster | Roadmaster Sedan, Roadmaster Estate Wagon, Roadmaster Limited | 5.7L LT1 V8 (Gen II)
records.title: LT1 intake manifold gasket coolant/oil leak
records.howToFix: Check and re-torque intake manifold bolts to spec first. If leaking persists, replace the intake manifold gaskets (and seals). Inspect for coolant contamination and top-end cleanliness during the job.
records.repairItems: Retorque/diagnose first; intake-manifold gasket set and seals if leakage persists
records.reason: The live page is in stock and states exact YMMT/engine fitment; the How to Fix calls for retorque before replacement.
records.correction: Keep retorque/inspection ahead of the parts CTA.

records.ymmt: 1994-1996 | Buick | Roadmaster | Roadmaster Sedan, Roadmaster Estate Wagon, Roadmaster Limited | 5.7L LT1 V8 (Gen II)
records.title: Optispark (Opti-Spark) distributor failure on the LT1
records.howToFix: Replace the Optispark with an AC Delco (vented) unit, and because the water pump has to come off to access it, replace the water pump at the same time. Ensure the distributor vent hoses are correctly routed and clear so condensation can escape. Rule out spark plug wires and plugs first, as those often mimic Optispark failure.
records.repairItems: Ignition diagnosis; vented Optispark distributor if confirmed; inspect/replace leaking water pump, hoses, plugs and wires as needed
records.reason: The live page is in stock with Add to Cart, identifies ACCEL 59125 and lists 1994-1996 Roadmaster; pin-drive/vented configuration still must be confirmed.
records.correction: Diagnose coil/wires/plugs first and inspect the water pump leak source before ordering.

records.ymmt: 1994-1996 | Buick | Roadmaster | Roadmaster Sedan, Roadmaster Estate Wagon, Roadmaster Limited | 5.7L LT1 V8 (Gen II)
records.title: Reverse-flow cooling: water pump shaft seal leak and air-lock overheating
records.howToFix: Replace the water pump (use special seal tool J39087 if only resealing, otherwise install a complete pump). When refilling coolant, open the bleeder screw on the thermostat housing to purge trapped air. Address any weep promptly to protect the Optispark below it.
records.repairItems: Water pump or specialist reseal using correct tool; coolant refill and LT1 bleed procedure
records.reason: The OEM page lists exact 1994-1996 Roadmaster 5.7L fitment.
records.correction: Do not imply the pump eliminates the required bleeding procedure or that resealing is appropriate without the specified tool.
